records.title: Payment requests carry an idempotency key
records.body: Every call that creates a charge sends an Idempotency-Key header generated once per user intent. The gateway stores the key with the response for 24 hours, so a client retry after a timeout returns the first result instead of charging the card twice.

records.title: The idempotency key must be reused on retry, not regenerated
records.body: A retry wrapper that builds a fresh UUID per attempt defeats the protection. Generate the key before the first attempt and pass the same value through every retry, including retries after a network timeout.

records.title: Reject a reused idempotency key that carries a different payload
records.body: If the same key arrives with a different amount or currency, answer 422 instead of replaying the old response. This catches client bugs early. Still being discussed with the mobile team.

records.title: Deduplicate charges by order id
records.body: Charges were deduplicated by order id with a unique index. It failed for split payments where one order has several charges, so it was replaced by per-request idempotency keys.

Customer charged twice after a gateway timeout. A 30 second timeout made the checkout retry the charge with a new request id. The first charge had succeeded, so the customer paid twice and support issued a refund. Root cause: no stable key across retries.

records.title: Hydration mismatch when rendering dates on the server
records.body: Formatting a date with the user locale and timezone gives different text on the server and in the browser, and React warns that hydration failed. Render a fixed UTC string on the server, then format in an effect after mount.

records.title: Use a ClientOnly wrapper for browser-dependent widgets
records.body: Components that read window, localStorage or the viewport width go inside the ClientOnly wrapper, which renders nothing on the server. This avoids the text content did not match errors.

records.title: Move date formatting to the API layer
records.body: Proposal: the API returns display-ready strings for dates so the frontend never formats them. Open question: it breaks per-user timezone preferences.

records.title: Suppress hydration warnings on date nodes
records.body: We used suppressHydrationWarning on every date element. It hid real bugs and the text still flickered, so it was dropped in favour of the ClientOnly wrapper.
Snapshot tests failed only in CI because the container used the en-US locale while developers used es-ES, so the rendered month names differed. Pinning the locale in the test setup fixed it.

records.title: Batch jobs exhaust the Postgres connection pool
records.body: Each worker opened its own pool of 20 connections, and with 15 workers the database hit max_connections and new jobs failed with too many clients. Size the pool as max_connections divided by worker count, and put pgbouncer in front.

records.title: Put pgbouncer in transaction mode in front of Postgres
records.body: All batch workers connect through pgbouncer in transaction pooling mode. Prepared statements must be disabled in the driver, because server connections are shared between transactions.

records.title: Set statement and idle timeouts per database role
records.body: Give the batch role a 5 minute statement timeout and a 30 second idle in transaction timeout so a stuck job releases its connection.

records.title: One shared pool per host
records.body: Run one process per host with a shared pool of 50 connections. Replaced when jobs moved to separate containers, since a pool cannot be shared across processes.

The nightly aggregation hung for two hours because a crashed worker kept 40 idle connections open. Postgres refused new sessions until the DBA terminated them by hand. We added idle_in_transaction_session_timeout afterwards.

records.title: Rotate refresh tokens on every use
records.body: Each refresh returns a new refresh token and invalidates the previous one. If an old refresh token is presented again we treat it as theft and revoke the whole token family, forcing a new login.

records.title: Concurrent tabs race on refresh token rotation
records.body: Two browser tabs refreshing at the same moment send the same refresh token; the second request looks like reuse and logs the user out. Allow a 10 second grace window for the previous token, or serialise refresh through a shared lock.

records.title: Shorten access token lifetime to 5 minutes
records.body: Reduce access token lifetime from 30 to 5 minutes to limit exposure. Needs the grace window above before rollout.

records.title: Long-lived refresh tokens without rotation
records.body: Refresh tokens lasted 90 days and were never rotated. Replaced by rotation after the security review.
After shipping the 10 second grace window for the previous refresh token, support tickets about users being logged out unexpectedly fell from about 40 a week to 3.

records.title: Terraform state lock left behind by a cancelled CI job
records.body: Cancelling a pipeline mid-apply leaves the DynamoDB lock held, and the next run fails with Error acquiring the state lock. Release it with terraform force-unlock only after confirming no apply is running.

records.title: Serialise terraform applies per environment in CI
records.body: The pipeline uses a concurrency group per environment so only one plan or apply runs at a time. Plans on pull requests run with -lock=false because they never write state.

records.title: Split the monolithic state by service
records.body: Break the single state file into one per service to shrink lock contention and blast radius. Migration with terraform state mv is risky and not scheduled.

records.title: Local state committed to the repository
records.body: State used to be a file in git. Replaced by a remote backend with locking after two engineers overwrote each other.
A cancelled apply held the state lock for 40 minutes during an incident, delaying a hotfix. We forced the unlock after checking the CI run history and the cloud audit log.

records.title: Gradle build cache poisoned by differing JDK versions
records.body: Developers on JDK 17 and CI on JDK 21 shared a remote build cache and got mysterious class file version errors. Include the JDK major version in the cache key or pin the toolchain in the build file.

records.title: Pin the Java toolchain in build.gradle
records.body: Declare the java toolchain languageVersion explicitly so every machine compiles with the same JDK, and let Gradle download it. Never rely on JAVA_HOME.

records.title: Enable the configuration cache for local builds
records.body: Turn on the Gradle configuration cache to cut incremental build time. Some plugins are still incompatible, so only enable it for the app module.

records.title: Clean build before every release
records.body: Run gradle clean before release builds to avoid stale outputs. Dropped once the toolchain pin made caching reliable, saving eight minutes per build.
After pinning the toolchain and trusting the remote cache the release pipeline went from 19 to 11 minutes. Cache hit rate rose to 84 percent.

records.title: Use cursor pagination for list endpoints
records.body: List endpoints return an opaque next_cursor built from the last sort key and id, instead of page numbers. Offset pagination skipped and duplicated rows whenever items were inserted while a client was paging.

records.title: The cursor must include a unique tiebreaker
records.body: Sorting by created_at alone drops rows that share a timestamp across a page boundary. Always append the primary key to the cursor and to the ORDER BY clause.

records.title: Cap page size at 100 and default to 25
records.body: Limit page size to protect the database; clients needing more should iterate.

records.title: Offset and limit pagination
records.body: Endpoints accepted page and per_page parameters. Replaced by cursors because deep pages made OFFSET scans slow.
A customer export using page numbers contained 37 duplicated orders because new orders arrived while it ran. Switching the export to cursor pagination fixed it.

records.title: Quarantine flaky tests instead of retrying the whole suite
records.body: A test that fails and then passes on rerun is tagged quarantine, runs in a separate non-blocking job and gets a ticket with a two week deadline. The main suite no longer retries.

records.title: Shared database state is the usual cause of flaky tests
records.body: Most flaky failures traced back to tests sharing rows or relying on execution order. Use a transaction per test with rollback, or a unique schema per xdist worker.

records.title: Report flake rate per test in the dashboard
records.body: Track the percentage of runs where each test flips result, to prioritise fixes.

records.title: Rerun failed tests three times
records.body: CI retried each failed test up to three times. It hid real regressions and tripled build time, so it was removed.
Two weeks after quarantining the 12 flakiest tests and isolating database state per worker, the main branch pipeline success rate moved from 71 to 93 percent.

records.title: Verify webhook signatures with a constant-time comparison
records.body: Compute the HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body with the shared secret and compare it using hmac.compare_digest. Never compare signatures with ==, which leaks timing information.

records.title: Verify the raw body, not the parsed JSON
records.body: Re-serialising parsed JSON changes whitespace and key order, so the HMAC no longer matches. Read the raw bytes before the framework parses the body.

records.title: Reject webhooks older than five minutes
records.body: Include a timestamp in the signed payload and refuse events older than 5 minutes to stop replay attacks.

records.title: Allowlist provider IP addresses
records.body: We trusted webhooks from a list of provider IPs. Replaced by signatures since the provider ranges changed without notice.
Valid webhooks were rejected after a logging middleware consumed and re-encoded the body, so every signature check failed for two hours and events were dropped until we replayed them.

records.title: Daily aggregates drift when grouped in the server timezone
records.body: Grouping by date in the database server timezone shifted late evening orders to the wrong day for customers in other regions. Store UTC, and convert to the customer timezone before truncating to a day.

records.title: Aggregate by customer-local day using AT TIME ZONE
records.body: Use created_at AT TIME ZONE customer_tz before date_trunc so daily totals match the customer calendar. Keep a tz column on the account.

records.title: Precompute daily buckets per timezone
records.body: Materialise totals per timezone nightly to make dashboards fast.

records.title: Report everything in Madrid time
records.body: All reports used Europe/Madrid. Replaced when customers outside Spain complained their totals were off.
Finance closed the month in UTC while the dashboard used local time, leaving a 12,400 euro difference in month-end revenue that took a day to explain. The dashboard now states its timezone.

records.title: Commit uv.lock and sync in CI with --frozen
records.body: The lockfile is committed. CI runs uv sync --frozen so a build fails instead of silently resolving newer versions.

records.title: uv run picks the wrong virtualenv when VIRTUAL_ENV is set
records.body: A stale VIRTUAL_ENV from another project makes uv warn and use a mismatched interpreter. Unset it with env -u VIRTUAL_ENV before running uv.

records.title: Use dependency groups for dev tools
records.body: Move linters and test tools into a dev dependency group instead of optional extras.

records.title: requirements.txt generated with pip-compile
records.body: Pins came from pip-compile. Replaced by uv lock, which resolves all platforms in one file.
Switching CI from pip to uv with a cached wheel directory cut dependency installation from 90 seconds to 6 seconds.

records.title: Every log line carries a correlation id
records.body: Generate a correlation id at the edge, put it in a context variable and add it to every structured log record. Propagate it in the X-Correlation-Id header to downstream calls.

records.title: Context variables are lost in thread pools
records.body: contextvars do not propagate into run_in_executor threads automatically, so logs from background work lose the correlation id. Copy the context explicitly with contextvars.copy_context().run.

records.title: Adopt OpenTelemetry trace ids as correlation ids
records.body: Reuse the trace id instead of a custom header once the collector is rolled out.

records.title: Plain text log lines with request prefixes
records.body: Logs were free text with a request number prefix. Replaced by JSON logs because grep over text was unreliable.
With correlation ids in logs, tracing a failed checkout across four services went from about 40 minutes to under 15, halving incident triage time.
